item.text:
**1B.1 Research Note: Andrés Manuel López Obrador in 2024**

I searched directly for 2024 evidence on nuclear disarmament, nonproliferation, escalation, and related existential-risk signaling. The 2024 record I found is overwhelmingly pro-disarmament and anti-escalation. I did not find reliable 2024 evidence that AMLO sought prestige, leverage, or personal power through nuclear escalation.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Mexico promotes peace at the eighth OPANAL course on nuclear disarmament and non-proliferation](https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/mexico-promotes-peace-at-the-eighth-opanal-course-on-nuclear-disarmament-and-non-proliferation?idiom=en) | Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores | 2024-01-26 | <https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/mexico-promotes-peace-at-the-eighth-opanal-course-on-nuclear-disarmament-and-non-proliferation?idiom=en> | Mexico’s foreign ministry supported a training course on nuclear disarmament and non-proliferation for officials from foreign affairs, defense, navy, and security, which is direct evidence of institutional effort to strengthen anti-nuclear knowledge rather than escalation. | 1B.1 |
| [Foreign Ministry prioritizes nuclear disarmament on Mexico’s international agenda](https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/foreign-ministry-prioritizes-nuclear-disarmament-on-mexico-s-international-agenda?idiom=en) | Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores | 2024-02-14 | <https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/foreign-ministry-prioritizes-nuclear-disarmament-on-mexico-s-international-agenda?idiom=en> | The foreign ministry explicitly framed Mexico’s diplomacy as working for a safer, more peaceful world based on international law and cooperation rather than weapons, at the 57th anniversary of the Treaty of Tlatelolco. This supports a risk-reduction interpretation. | 1B.1 |
| [With World at Delicate Crossroads, Disarmament Committee’s Responsibility ‘Immense’, Says General Assembly President During Robust Debate](https://press.un.org/en/2024/gadis3737.doc.htm) | United Nations, Meetings Coverage and Press Releases | 2024-10-08 | <https://press.un.org/en/2024/gadis3737.doc.htm> | In the First Committee debate, Mexico’s representative urged progress on nuclear disarmament, fewer warheads, less rhetoric threatening nuclear use, and rejected the idea that nuclear weapons are part of the solution. This is the clearest 2024 multilateral statement showing AMLO’s government pushing existential-risk reduction. | 1B.1 |

**Bottom line**

- Best-supported reading: AMLO’s government in 2024 publicly aligned with nuclear-risk reduction, disarmament, and opposition to nuclear threats.
- I found no credible 2024 evidence of AMLO pursuing nuclear escalation, nuclear brinkmanship, or existential-risk increase for prestige or leverage.
- The evidence is mostly diplomatic and rhetorical, not operational. That makes the case for “seeking to reduce existential risk” real but limited in scope.

**Search gap**

- I used direct searches across Mexican government sources, UN materials, and broader news/disarmament queries.
- The gap is specific: I did not find a 2024 Mexico-specific escalatory act or statement tied to nuclear risk, because Mexico is not a nuclear-armed state and the available 2024 record centers on disarmament, treaty commemoration, and anti-threat language.
- If a later stage needs stronger counterevidence, it will likely have to come from non-nuclear domains, not this lens.
